head.title: Request a Quote | Margo Rubber Products, Nashik India

paragraphs: Margo Rubber Products quotes moulded and extruded rubber components from a drawing, a specification or a worn sample. Acknowledgement within one business day; quotation and feasibility report inside 48 hours, with a compound recommendation and a lead time.

fields.label: Chips ×3
fields.note: MOQ 500 PCS is the most prominent MOQ statement on the site — a chip, above the fold, on the page where a buyer decides whether to enquire. Standing founder instruction, 2026-08-19: never publish a piece count. 30+ countries is a seventh distinct country count across the site; the others are 60+, 50+, 27+, 25+, eight, and zero

notes: Heading. Page’s only <h1>, three <span class="block"> children.

Keyword. This page targets bottom-funnel intent — rubber components RFQ India, request quote rubber manufacturer. It does not need a head term in the H1; it needs the verb the buyer is about to perform. “Send a drawing” is that verb.
Chips are <li> in a <ul>, not headings, and set uppercase in CSS rather than typed in caps.

Consistency gate. 48 hours for the quotation, one business day for acknowledgement — the same two strings on every page. Live, this page says “1 business day” in the hero and its own footer says “within 24 hours”, 1,500px apart.

notes: Crawlability is already correct here, and that is worth protecting. All four selects and their 40-odd options render in the DOM before step 1 is completed — verified. This is the only progressive-disclosure component on the site that does not unmount. Do not "optimise" it.

Every option string is content. Eleven product categories and nine industries in the DOM of the RFQ page is a real semantic signal about what Margo makes — which is why the two missing categories cost more than a dropdown gap.
Selects need <label>, not just a first option acting as one. “Select country” as option[value=""] is fine as a placeholder, but the accessible name must come from a real bound label.
Do not make PHONE required. It is optional on step 1 and should stay so — an overseas buyer at the enquiry stage will abandon rather than hand over a number.
Schema. None on this section. Do not attempt to mark up the form itself.

fields.label: What happens next
fields.note: Five rows, all sourced. This is the single highest-value block that could be added to the page: it answers the question every RFQ visitor has, it is unique to Margo, and no Indian competitor in the teardown publishes it

fields.label: Three FAQ entries
rows: What if we have no drawing?
Send the physical part. Margo measures it, identifies the compound family and quotes against the sample. A large share of the work starts as a worn component in an envelope rather than a CAD file.
What information does a quotation need?
The application, the operating temperature, the media in contact and any standard the drawing calls out. Those four inputs are what make a compound recommendation possible inside 48 hours.
Do you quote against a minimum order?
Margo produces in bulk — minimum run from 10,000 pieces per part number, or quoted against the part on larger sections. Tell us the part and the volume and we will quote it.
fields.note: Three entries, 40–50 words each, with a FAQPage node. Adds roughly 800px, real AEO surface, and answers the three objections that stop an RFQ being sent. The third replaces the MOQ question rather than dodging it — it is the founder’s own phrasing from the company profile commercial terms

notes: These additions roughly double the page. 2,262px is not a length problem in itself — it is a signal that the page answers almost none of the questions a visitor arrives with. Every block above is sourced and already written somewhere in Margo’s own material.
